name: True Fire Skull
blurb: The one every airbrush artist paints first and never stops painting. Real true-fire technique, white-hot cores bleeding to feathered orange tips.

name: Respirator
blurb: Skull in a twin-cartridge spray respirator with the fire glow behind it. For anyone who has spent a summer masked up in a hot booth.

name: Flaming Piston
blurb: A chrome piston climbing out of its own fire. The other half of the trade: the engine the paint goes on.

name: Screaming Skull
blurb: Jaw wrenched open mid-scream in a burst of flung paint, drips running off the mandible. The loudest thing on the rack.

name: Ghost Flame
blurb: Ghost flames and fine pinstriping over a skull that only shows where the light catches it. For when you do not want to shout.

name: Crossed Airbrushes
blurb: Skull and crossbones, except the bones are two gravity-feed airbrushes trailing mist. The closest thing this trade has to a flag.

name: Airbrush ER
blurb: A workshop badge for the emergency room. Because most of owning an airbrush is diagnosing one.

name: Anatomy Plate
blurb: The patient on the table, labelled like a medical chart: nozzle, needle, trigger, cup. Everything that goes wrong, in order.

name: Exploded View
blurb: One airbrush taken fully apart and floating on its axis. If you have ever lost a nozzle on a workshop floor, this is your shirt.

name: AirbrushDOC
blurb: The mark and the promise, set in overspray. Cures for your canvas.

name: True Fire Wrap
blurb: A wall of true fire running the whole way round the mug. Coffee optional, flames mandatory.
